A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ICTSP research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting experiments, architectural ablations, synthetic-data analyses and repeated-seed results in Section 3 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds experiments on restricted history, filling strategies, model reduction and context contributions in Appendices A.6–A.11.

M1.justification: The core ICTSP architecture, token retrieval and training objective are retained. Appendix A.6 introduces limited input-handling adaptations: ICTSP (Limited) permits incomplete forecasting-task tokens with mean-filled history, and another variant replaces the original few-shot zero filling with mean filling.

E1.justification: The ETT, Weather, Electricity, Traffic and synthetic Multi datasets are retained. Coverage extends modestly to forecasting with temporally separated, distant context and combined-source ETT transfer in A.10–A.11, without introducing a new application domain.

E2.justification: Tables 1–9 retain their comparator sets. Tables 13 and 15 add linear/NLinear-equivalent and MLP-only comparison controls on Weather and ETTm2; v1's linear-only warm-up comparison was on ECL. Newly cited ForecastPFN and AutoTimes are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: Original evaluation settings are retained, but substantial new controlled protocols are added: retaining only 512 observed steps with Lb = 336, comparing filling strategies, varying random context retention, sampling distant context from a 4096-step history, and evaluating channel-specific context under single-source and combined-source training.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's context, retrieval, sampling-step and warm-up analyses, v2 tests whether performance depends on longer visible history, padding choices, linear versus MLP components, context quantity and distance, and the channel supplying context. Tables 11–18 substantially expand evidence about ICTSP's mechanisms and robustness.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same default seed and five-seed Weather/ECL analysis using seeds 2022–2026 in A.3.2 and Figure 8. The additional experiments do not introduce new repeated-run counts, uncertainty estimates or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 1–9 are unchanged, but v2 adds substantial variant-specific and diagnostic results. For example, Table 12 reports 10% ETTm2 average MSE of 0.264 with mean filling versus 0.275 with zero filling; Table 17 reports 0.208 without context versus 0.168 with full context for ETTm1-to-ETTm2 transfer. These are additional comparisons, not revised same-setting headline scores.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11 and the existing mathematical formulation are retained. The new feature-space explanation and model-reduction discussion provide conceptual interpretation and experimental motivation, without adding formal assumptions, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: forecasting-task tokenization enables ICL, addresses existing Transformer weaknesses, supports adaptive model reduction and performs strongly across full-data, few-shot and zero-shot settings.

C2.justification: v2 distinguishes aligned from shifted inter-series dependencies and develops a feature-space explanation in A.8. It also attributes padding effects to interaction with last-value demeaning and explicitly acknowledges in A.11.1 that full-data context improvements cannot isolate ICL from relationships already encoded in model weights. These substantially extend the original interpretations and qualifications.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-implementation link on the first page and specifies how to construct the new masking, filling, context-selection and combined-training experiments. The original optimizer, hardware, batch sizes, preprocessing and principal hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Müller et al. on Bayesian inference, ForecastPFN, AutoTimes and Xing et al. ForecastPFN and AutoTimes receive brief connections to the tokenization discussion. The broader positioning against existing forecasting Transformers and LLM adaptations is retained.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact. Changes include a localized expansion of the series-wise Transformer explanation, additional appendix subsections, author-year citations and conference header text. The scientific additions do not entail wholesale rewriting of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds the architectural comparison matrix in Table 10 and eight experimental tables, including channel-specific result matrices. Existing figures and tables are retained but reflowed under the conference template; Tables 7 and 8 are grouped on one page. This substantially expands and reorganizes the tabular presentation.

improvement.justification: The matched-history, filling-strategy and context-contribution controls address questions that v1's original ablations left open, while the code link improves reproducibility information. These benefits are tempered by reporting problems: A.6 claims superiority in all experiments despite ties and losses in Table 12, and Table 18's training-source caption conflicts with A.11.3. The additional evidence provides a positive but qualified overall improvement.
